correctness.rationale: Anisotropic conditional Gaussian mixture gives even spatial moments from powers of a bounded additive cosine functional. The angular reset generator fixes pi_n=r nu_n/(r+4D_rot n²). Small-time top harmonics prove necessity; a finite closed triangular ODE and induction prove sufficiency at all positive times. Toeplitz Gram factorization gives N>=m+1 with equality iff uniform regular axes. Stationary angular covariance integrates exactly to H(t) and the fourth cumulant; the stationary third angular harmonic gives the nonzero sixth-order small-time direction difference. Formula boundaries D_rot,r,d0>0, 0<|delta|<d0, and stationarity are explicit. Program checks 103 finite numerical/algebraic assertions, not a substitute for these general proofs.

originality.rationale: Primary original work arXiv:2406.17550v2, particularly Sections II, V, and VI, gives the anisotropic colloid model and fixed-angle resetting second moments; no arbitrary reset-law all-orders finite-time directional-moment theorem is in the inspected relevant sections. arXiv:2501.05149v1 Section III.3 is an active anisotropic particle with fixed orientational resets, not the claimed passive sharp hierarchy. The minimum support lemma is a known circle quadrature consequence, explicitly not claimed as new; the scientific finding is the dynamical if-and-only-if transfer to displacement moments, its sharp protocol interpretation, and the explicit fourth/sixth cumulant diagnostics. Extensive semantic search did not surface a matching dynamic theorem, but negative searches do not prove novelty and a general moment-functional theorem could subsume some aspects.
residual_risks: A sufficiently broad general theorem for additive functionals of angular Markov processes or Gaussian scale mixtures might already imply the finite-time harmonic hierarchy as a corollary; independent literature confirmation remains warranted.
Static minimum-support regular angular designs are classical consequences of trigonometric quadrature and are not independently novel.
Only the relevant sections of the 2024 active-resetting model, the 2025 follow-up and the introduction of the 2010 quadrature work were scrutinized, not all supplemental appendices of every work.
No independent scientific audit or rigorously certified floating-point error bounds were obtained.

value.rationale: A shape-anisotropic Brownian colloid may have isotropic displacement covariance while concealing higher spatial cumulant anisotropies. The result provides a sharp, all-times resource law for the number and arrangement of independently sampled orientation-reset axes necessary to suppress anisotropy through a selected order, proves no finite palette can erase all moment anisotropy, and exhibits an explicit strictly non-Gaussian fourth cumulant and sixth-order leakage. This resolves a natural control/identification gap left by single-orientation reset transport calculations and is not an arbitrary finite slice. The already-known unit-circle quadrature extremizer is integrated with a genuinely dynamic finite-time criterion, not presented as new by itself.
